## 1. Background: Western Europe, 1945–1947

### 1.1 Postwar physical devastation and damaged infrastructure
Sustained aerial bombing badly damaged most major European cities, and industry was hit hard. Transport suffered especially: railways, bridges, and docks were targeted, and much merchant shipping was sunk  [Marshall Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Plan). Most wartime belligerents had also exhausted their treasuries  [Marshall Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Plan).

### 1.2 Food and fuel shortages
The US shipped 16.5 million tons of food to Europe and Japan between July 1945 and June 1946, mostly wheat, and shortages were severe, especially in the winter of 1946–47  [Marshall Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Plan). The western zones of Germany were hit hardest. They reached only about 50% of prewar food self-sufficiency, food output ran 30% below prewar levels in 1946–48, and industrial output fell by more than half, regaining prewar levels only at the end of 1949  [Marshall Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Plan). The supplied material does not address fuel shortages specifically.

# Report on Everything: A Scoped, Cited Overview of Global Developments Through Late 2026

## 1. Executive Summary

**Scope and purpose.** "Everything" cannot be covered in one report. This document is a broad, multi-domain overview for a general-but-informed reader, covering developments through late 2026 with context from the prior decade. Coverage is uneven because of the evidence available. Economics, global risk, climate, demographics and AI are covered with sourced material. Science, health and culture are largely unsourced and are flagged as gaps rather than filled with unverified claims.
